description:
FILED s473t5a (#1501 CHECK 1 round 2, 2026-09-13).  t/op/decl-refs.t: P 402/0,
C 42/165 -- 195 rows never produced, behind TWO refusals inside code the file
evals with `eval $code or die $@`, so a refusal is a DIE that aborts the whole
enclosing top-level `for` loop.  This task is the FIRST of the two; #1649 is the
second.

MINIMAL REPRODUCER (perl 5.40.3 accepts it; PCL refuses the FILE):

    use feature 'declared_refs', 'state';
    no warnings 'experimental::declared_refs';
    my @ret;
    @ret = state (\($d, $e));
    print "ok\n";

    perl: ok
    pcl : Parser2 TODO: state outside a block-level declaration

The trigger is a `state` declarator that is NOT the head of its statement, with
a Structure::List after it.  `Pl/Parser2.pm:7282` requires the declarator's
enclosing statement to be a `PPI::Statement::Variable` whose parent is a Block
or the Document; `@ret = state (…)` is a plain `PPI::Statement`, so it dies.

WHAT DOES *NOT* REPRODUCE (probed, all fine today): `my $ret = state \$a;`
(statement-head), `$z = state $w;` (a bare Symbol after the declarator -- the
walk's `$nx` test admits only Symbol or Structure::List and this one takes the
Symbol path), `$ret = state \\$i;` (a Cast follows the word, so the walk skips
it), and the same shapes inside a string eval.  So it is specifically
mid-statement `state (LIST)`.

HOW THE 195 ROWS SIT BEHIND IT.  decl-refs.t runs two loops over
declarator x sigil and evals a ~50-line program per pair with `eval $code or
die $@`.  The FIRST heredoc's 12 pairs are (my, state, our, local) x ($, @, %)
in that order: `my` x 3 transpile, `state` hits this refusal, the die kills the
outer loop, and the SECOND heredoc's 9 pairs go with it (they hit #1649
regardless).  Rows 1..207 are loop 1 (which does not die) plus the three `my`
iterations; 195 is the rest.  Measured per pair by extracting the heredocs and
transpiling each: `scratch/s473t5a/probe/gen-declrefs.pl` in the s473t5a
worktree writes the 21 programs and `try-declrefs.sh` prints the verdicts --
h1-{my,our,local}-{S,A,H} OK, h1-state-{S,A,H} this refusal, all nine h2-* #1649.

SIZE: 195 rows of t/op/decl-refs.t, shared with #1649 (both must be fixed for
the file to run to its end).  The shortfall row's cause names both.

=== s543s NOTE (2026-11-24, the round, phase 1; Opus 5.5) -- six rows keyed here are POSITIONAL pairs, moved by s543h ===
Six of perl's never-produced `state` rows of t/op/decl-refs.t (209 211 213 215 217 219) went ok -> not ok at s543h (MAIN-READY-107; companion one-file MR-106 74/151 -> MR-107 68/157; main -108 68/157).  They are POSITIONAL pairs: this refusal aborts the first heredoc loop (t-lines 41-106) at its `state` iteration, so perl's rows 208-225 have no PCL row of their description and the aligner (tools/lib/PclTapAlign.pm, "no evidence: as-is") pairs them by NUMBER with PCL's rows 208-225 = the LAST loop's 18 `for my|state|our \~x (\~::y)` rows (perl's 385-402).
Those PCL rows fail since s543h for a reason outside this task: the declarator loop's `eval "for our \$x (\$y) {}"` (and @, %; t-line 16), which perl REFUSES at compile time ("Experimental aliasing via reference not enabled": refaliasing is enabled only at t-line 108), RUNS in PCL (no feature gate = the file's NS:Error-compatibility rows) and since s543h aliases $::x / @::x / %::x to ~::y as perl does with the feature on (the alias outlives the loop in perl too).  Before s543h a `for our \$x (...)` inside a string eval did not alias the package variable at all (a silent wrong that s543h's name resolution fixed), so the six rows passed ON that silent wrong.  The two values `isnt \$x, \$::x` compared: perl SCALAR(0x..bd8) vs SCALAR(0x..0e0) ok; MR-106 SCALAR(0x1) vs SCALAR(0x2) ok; MR-107 SCALAR(0x1) vs SCALAR(0x1) not ok.
Reproducer (perl -> MR-106 -> MR-107):
    use feature 'declared_refs'; no warnings 'experimental::declared_refs';
    for my $funny (qw< $ @ % >) {
        eval "for our \\${funny}x (\\${funny}y) {}";
        print "eval $funny: ", ($@ ? "died: $@" : "ran\n");
    }
    use feature 'refaliasing'; no warnings 'experimental::refaliasing';
    print \$::x == \$::y ? "not ok - \$::x is \$::y\n" : "ok - \$::x is not \$::y\n";
  perl:          eval $: died: Experimental aliasing via reference not enabled at (eval 1) line 1. ... ok - $::x is not $::y
  MR-106 b58114ca: eval $: ran ... ok - $::x is not $::y
  MR-107 0eb941e3 (and main -108): eval $: ran ... not ok - $::x is $::y
  (with `use feature 'refaliasing'` BEFORE the eval perl aliases too: MR-106 did not, MR-107 does -- round2/declrefs/e-forour.pl.)
In-file confirmation: the file cut to its declarator loop + the last loop (round2/declrefs/s1.pl) shows the six rows ok on MR-106, not ok on MR-107; the same cut WITHOUT the `for $decl \~x (\~y) {}` spelling (s2.pl) shows them ok on both.
WHEN THIS TASK IS FIXED: the positional pairs go away (the six rows keyed here leave), and perl's own rows 386 388 390 392 394 396 ("\~x is not equivalent to \~::x", for my / for state) will be produced at their numbers and FAIL for the alias reason above -- an invalid-input divergence (principle 9: the eval perl refuses runs), to be keyed NS:Error-compatibility, not a regression of the fix.  Rows keyed: baselines/perl-suite-fails.tsv op/decl-refs.t 209-219 odd (s543s).  Files: ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s543/round2/declrefs/.
subject: `state (LIST)` used MID-STATEMENT ("@ret = state (\($d,$e));") refuses the whole file -- "Parser2 TODO: state outside a block-level declaration"; t/op/decl-refs.t's 195 rows
